summary: I sent the exact prompt. The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review, read the code-reviewer.md template and sent a general-purpose reviewer subagent over a13c251..3f86a49 using the Agent tool. The subagent ran the code to confirm two Critical defects: the pagination offset (handlers.js:18) and the unawaited saveOrder (handlers.js:37). It answered "Ready to merge? No". It made no blocking claims about any of the listed correct code. The parent agent checked the findings itself and reported "do not merge — 2 Critical defects".
reasoning: All 12 criteria pass, so the overall verdict is pass. The skill was invoked and the review went through the Agent tool to a subagent. Both target defects were flagged as Critical with file:line references and a concrete input and outcome, and the merge was not approved. Every item the story lists as correct code was either praised or mentioned only as a Minor point. Each Important finding also names a trigger and what happens as a result.

observations.description: On first launch, the workspace-trust dialog and the bypass-permissions warning both default to 'No, exit'. To get through, the tester has to press Down and then Enter on each one.

After the reviewer finished, the parent agent re-checked the findings and ran extra steps: the receiving-code-review skill, a Codex gate preflight, and an ungated-ledger append. Because of this, the final summary is the parent's rewrite of the review, not the subagent's text quoted as-is. It also put a codex-plugin install notice at the top of the review, which is noise for this user. The whole run took about 4 minutes ('Cogitated for 4m 11s').

Important #5 contains a contestable claim: the parent's summary says 'nowIso sits in src/util.js:3 unused', but the test file uses a fixed clock, so this point may be arguable. The test fixture itself was not flagged as a defect.

The agent's skill paths point to a different worktree (/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/.worktrees/a1-rerun-treatment/...). CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT was apparently unset, so the agent had to search for the codex-preflight script itself.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched a reviewer subagent via Agent tool
criteria.evidence: The session log tool_use entries were: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}, then Read code-reviewer.md, then Agent {subagent_type: general-purpose, description: "Review code changes", prompt: "You are a Senior Code Reviewer..."}. The subagent log is subagents/agent-a662cea12266a8645.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Pagination offset in listOrdersHandler flagged under Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under the subagent's 'Critical (Must Fix)' heading: '1. src/handlers.js:18 — off-by-one offset: page 1 silently skips the first page of orders... It must be (page - 1) * size'. The final screen also showed 'Critical 1 — pagination offset is off by one'.

criteria.criterion: Unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler flagged under Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under the Critical heading: '2. src/handlers.js:37 — store.saveOrder is async but is called without await: the handler returns 201 for orders it did not save, and the rejection crashes the process.' The subagent confirmed this by running it: 'handler returned: {"status":201...} orders stored: 0'.

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: The subagent said 'Ready to merge? No'. The parent agent said '## Verdict: do not merge — 2 Critical defects'.

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding asserts a defect in the listed correct items (header)
criteria.evidence: The Critical/Important findings were #1 offset, #2 unawaited save, #3 duplicate ids, #4 tests assert shape not content, #5 no body validation on create. None of them targets the listed items (see 6–11).
The Strengths section says 'withRetry is correctly written'. The only other mention is Minor #6: 'the retry wrapper around store.listOrders cannot ever help'.
It is mentioned only in Minor #8: 'src/config.js:3-9 / config.json — scope deviation worth confirming... It is not harmful'.
The Strengths section says 'parseOrderId is the right shape... returning null rather than throwing, with the handler translating null into a 400'.
The Strengths section says 'Pagination state stays out of the store. store.listOrders(offset, limit)... That's the correct seam.' No blocking finding targets it.
